summary: Social V2 Phase 1 tested end-to-end on the shared backend + web (/social, /social/room/:id) + mobile Expo preview. Backend: 7/8 pytest cases pass. Friend graph is fully working: search, request, accept, GET /api/social/friends returns friends+incoming+outgoing+counts, and /api/social/home reflects the new friend count. Rooms: create/list/join/leave, messages (empty rejected 400), reactions, playback host-guard (403 for non-host, 200 for host), and room-not-found (404) all pass. HEARTBEAT HAS A CRITICAL BUG: POST /api/social/rooms/{id}/heartbeat returns 500 on the SECOND call when a FRIEND is present, because `_award_listen_challenge` reads `last_credit_at` back from Mongo as tz-naive datetime and subtracts it from `_now()` which is tz-aware (`TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`, /app/backend/routes/social_v2.py:535). First heartbeat works (last==None branch); every subsequent friend-present heartbeat 500s. This breaks the Listen Together challenge minute-counter entirely and makes the room polling loop error every 2.5s from the client. Web /social: all testids render (social-v2, social-happening-now, social-tabs, social-tab-* for together/live/moments/clubs/friends, social-together, social-start-room, do-together grid). Live/Moments/Clubs render social-coming-soon. Friends tab (social-friends) shows social-friend-search that populates social-search-results (found freeuser@ ✓) and shows the accepted friend inline. V2 header 'Social' nav points to /social. Persistent mini-player stays mounted. Mobile Expo (demo login via 'Try the demo' testID demo-login-btn): social-screen, social-together, social-tabs, social-tab-* all render; social-start-room visible; Live tab shows social-coming-soon; Friends tab shows social-friend-search. Live listening rooms card renders on mobile with the two seed rooms created by the backend tests. PARITY: friend graph is genuinely shared — the demo⇄freeuser friendship created via web-side API is visible on both surfaces. Mobile 'happening_now.live_experiences' counter displays 0 while the same session's live rooms list shows 2 rows — this is not a parity bug, it's the 40s participant-presence cutoff vs the 120s room-listing cutoff (documented eventual-consistency, ≤2.5s per spec).

critical.issue: TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes at social_v2.py:535 (_award_listen_challenge). MongoDB returns `last_credit_at` as naive datetime, `_now()` is tz-aware. Every heartbeat call AFTER the first while a friend is present returns 500. This bricks the Listen Together challenge progress AND the room polling loop (client sees 500 every 2.5s once >1 friend joins).

minor.issue: happening_now.live_experiences uses the 40s participant-presence window, but rooms are still LISTED in suggested_rooms for up to 120s (ROOM_ACTIVE_SEC*3). This produces a jarring UI state where 'Live now: 0' shows above a list containing 2 live rooms. Consider unifying the two cutoffs or letting live_experiences match suggested_rooms.

action_items: HIGH: Fix social_v2.py:535 — force `last_credit_at` to tz-aware before subtracting. Either store as ISO string like `playback.updated_at` does, or normalise: `last = last.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) if last and last.tzinfo is None else last`. Same fix needed on the first heartbeat write ($set last_credit_at=_now()) so subsequent Mongo reads round-trip correctly. Motor by default does NOT return tz-aware datetimes — need CodecOptions(tz_aware=True) OR normalise on read.
MEDIUM: Consider aligning ROOM_ACTIVE_SEC (40) with the room-listing cutoff (120s = ROOM_ACTIVE_SEC*3) so /home counters don't undercount active rooms.
critical_code_review_comments: social_v2.py:535 — datetime subtraction is unsafe against Motor's default naive-datetime read. This is the exact same pattern that would break `last_active_at` comparisons elsewhere if they were subtracted the same way (currently they're only used inside Mongo queries via $gte {datetime}, which Motor serializes correctly, so those are safe).

social_v2.py:405 — `list_rooms` filters out rooms where `not parts and host_user_id != uid`. Freshly-created rooms depend on the host's participant record being present within ROOM_ACTIVE_SEC (40s). If a host creates a room but no client heartbeats within 40s, the room disappears from listings for OTHERS while still appearing to the host. This may cause 'room I created is invisible' friction in slow-network scenarios.

social_v2.py:88-93 — `_user_public` derives `name` from email local-part when no name; this is what surfaces 'Free' as 'Free Tester' etc. Fine, but note it also leaks users' full names in /users/search results with no visibility filter (mutual friends, city, etc.). Consider adding a `is_public_searchable` flag before broad rollout.

SocialV2.jsx:151-172 — startRoom() silently no-ops when nothing is playing (toast.info) — good UX. But `content` is passed straight from importedStation without whitelisting fields; the whole station snapshot is persisted in Mongo rooms.content. Could bloat if the station object grew.

ListenRoom.jsx:59-84 — every heartbeat error is swallowed as 'transient'. Because of the 500 bug above, the room will silently fail to update presence/messages/challenge on subsequent polls with no user-facing signal. At minimum log to console.warn so the bug is discoverable in prod telemetry.

success_rate.backend: 7/8 pytest (87.5%); 1 critical failure on heartbeat delta
success_rate.frontend: 100% of testid + coming-soon + tab-switch checks on both web and mobile

rca of the issue: PyMongo/Motor by default deserialise BSON datetimes as *naive* Python datetimes (UTC values, but with tzinfo=None). The Social V2 code writes `last_credit_at: _now()` where `_now()` returns `datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (tz-aware). On write PyMongo drops the tzinfo during BSON encoding. On the very next heartbeat we read that document back and try `(now - last)` where `now` is tz-aware and `last` is naive → TypeError → 500. Fix options: (a) Configure the AsyncIOMotorClient with `tz_aware=True` (may have ripple effects elsewhere), (b) locally normalise on read: `last = last.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc) if last and last.tzinfo is None else last`, or (c) store ISO strings like the existing `playback.updated_at` already does. Option (b) is the smallest safe change.
